extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institutions, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, advisors, and higher-education attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for postsecondary institutions' Title IX grievance hearings, with emphasis on cross-examination, relevance determinations, trauma-informed practices, training, impartiality, and protections for participation or refusal to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must determine relevance before answering
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a party or witness answers a cross-examination question, the decision-maker must determine if the question is relevant (§106.45(b)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This built-in “pause” ensures cross-examination remains focused on relevant questions, prevents abusive or harassing questions from being posed, and helps ensure the pace of cross-examination does not place undue pressure on a party or witness to answer immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination conducted only by party advisors (no self-representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination must be conducted by each party's advisor rather than by the parties themselves; the final regulations do not grant a right of self-representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having advisors perform cross-examination preserves recipient impartiality (the recipient observes advocacy but does not conduct it), equalizes procedural opportunity between parties, and avoids risks of ineffectiveness or trauma from a perpetrator personally cross-examining a victim.

rubrics_metrics.name: If party/witness refuses cross-examination, decision-maker may not rely on their statement but may decide based on remaining evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party or witness does not submit to cross-examination at the hearing, the decision-maker must not rely on any statement of that party or witness in reaching a determination regarding responsibility; however, the decision-maker cannot draw any inference about responsibility based solely on absence or refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision-maker may reach a determination based on the remaining evidence so long as no inference is drawn based on the party or witness's absence from the hearing or refusal to answer cross-examination or other questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must explain written reasons for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers are required to explain in writing the reasons for determinations regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written explanation helps ensure accountability, provides grounds for appeal if a decision-maker inappropriately applied pre-existing assumptions amounting to bias, and addresses concerns that a neutral hearing officer might improperly exclude questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-makers must be well-trained to serve impartially and avoid bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure decision-makers are trained to serve impartially, including how to avoid prejudgment of facts and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must comply with §106.45(b)(1)(iii) and can include trauma-informed approaches so long as training materials avoid sex stereotypes, do not prejudge facts of specific cases, and cover issues of relevance (including application of rape-shield protections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility determinations based on multiple factors (not demeanor alone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility should be assessed based on factors such as specific detail, inherent plausibility, internal consistency, corroborative evidence, and demeanor — but not solely on demeanor because it is an unreliable indicator of truthfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination brings to the decision-maker's attention factors like inconsistency and plausibility that other devices may not; decision-makers should evaluate answers in context and consider trauma, stress, effects of substances, and normal fallibility of memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must control hearing environment and prevent abusive questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are responsible for controlling a hearing environment to keep proceedings focused on relevant evidence and ensure participants are treated respectfully so the process will not be weaponized for or against any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may design rules (applied equally to both parties) to ensure no party is questioned in an abusive or intimidating manner, may grant breaks for panic attacks or flashbacks, and may require parties to be in separate rooms during live hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed practices are permitted but must not lead to prejudgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to include trauma-informed approaches in training and investigatory practices, provided such training complies with §106.45(b)(1)(iii) and does not apply generalizations about trauma to specific cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: investigators can offer parties opportunities to make statements under trauma-informed approaches prior to cross-examination; decision-makers should evaluate non-linear recall in context and allow breaks when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-recorded testimony is not an adequate substitute for live cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department disagrees that allowing pre-recorded testimony in lieu of answering questions during a live hearing would sufficiently accomplish the function of cross-examination in the postsecondary context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-recorded testimony does not permit real-time follow-up to challenge inconsistencies and inaccuracies; the regulations instead allow parties to be in separate rooms during live hearings to mitigate direct contact without eliminating live questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials must avoid reliance on sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) forbids training materials for Title IX personnel from relying on sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-maker and personnel training should specifically address avoidance of sex stereotypes and rape myths; trauma-informed material may be included only if it promotes impartiality and does not lead to prejudgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-retaliation protections for participation or refusal to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71 prohibits retaliation and provides that no recipient or person may intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate against any individual for exercising Title IX rights, including participation or refusal to participate in a Title IX proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must protect individuals from retaliation for filing reports, assisting, participating, or refusing to participate in investigations, proceedings, or hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination serves truth-seeking by surfacing inconsistencies and multiple viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination brings important factors (inconsistency, plausibility, corroboration) to a decision-maker in a way other procedural devices may not, because it is conducted by someone whose purpose is to advance one side's perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When each side is represented by an advisor, the decision-maker hears relevant evidence from all viewpoints and is more likely to reach a determination reflecting the truth of the allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layperson officials can make relevance and credibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department believes determinations about whether questions or evidence are relevant or directly related to allegations can reasonably be made by layperson recipient officials applying logic and common sense; legal training is not required for these factual determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: assessing credibility based on plausibility, consistency, and corroboration are functions traditionally performed by jurors; recipients should still provide training to avoid bias and prejudgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must explain reasons for excluding questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed/required practice: if a decision-maker excludes a question, the decision-maker must explain the reasons for exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural transparency is intended to address concerns that a neutral hearing officer might improperly filter or refuse to ask a party's questions and to ensure fairness in question exclusion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supportive measures to complainants (and encourage for respondents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer complainants supportive measures regardless of whether a formal complaint is filed, and the regulations encourage offering supportive measures for respondents as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures and other accommodations can mitigate harms of participation in the grievance process and are part of protections afforded by the final regulations.
